# Enterprise controls

## Scope

Applies when the change touches a product whose `.aidd/config.yaml` sets `project.compliance` targets or uses the audited profile. Or code that implements sign-in, SSO, SCIM, MFA, sessions, audit logs, an admin console, or another control an enterprise buyer or an auditor asks about. Not when compliance is off and no sign-in, session, admin, or audit path changes. Neighbours: `aidd-team:secure-coding`, `aidd-team:threat-model`, `aidd-team:incident-response`.

## Standards

| # | Standard | Edition | Checked | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S1 | SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (CC6 logical access, CC7 system operations, CC8 change management, A1 availability, C1 confidentiality) | 2017, with the 2022 revised points of focus | 2026-10-16 | <https://www.aicpa-cima.com/resources/download/2017-trust-services-criteria-with-revised-points-of-focus-2022> |
| S2 | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A, the technological controls (8.x) and the incident controls (5.24 to 5.28) | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 with Amd 1:2024 | 2026-10-16 | <https://www.iso.org/standard/27001> |
| S3 | GDPR Art. 25 (data protection by design and by default), Art. 32 (security of processing), and Art. 33 and 34 (breach notification) | Regulation (EU) 2016/679 | 2026-10-16 | <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj> |
| S4 | OWASP ASVS 5.0: Level 1 by default, Level 2 for authentication, session, and admin surfaces when compliance is on | 5.0.0 | 2026-10-16 | <https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/releases/tag/v5.0.0_release> |
| S5 | NIST SSDF (SP 800-218) | SP 800-218 v1.1 | 2026-10-16 | <https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final> |
| S6 | Least-privilege CI: OIDC federation over long-lived secrets, actions pinned by commit SHA | — | 2026-10-16 | <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/openid-connect> |
| S7 | SBOM in CycloneDX (with ML-BOM) or SPDX, and VEX | 1.7.2 | 2026-10-16 | <https://github.com/CycloneDX/specification/releases/tag/1.7.2> |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | Read `project.compliance`. With compliance on (any target, or the audited profile), name the controls the change touches (EC-01 to EC-19 in `references/controls.md`) in the Spec's Context. With it off, only this pack's triggers load it. | S1, S2 |
| Specify | A change on a security or auth path links a threat model and an authorization matrix; with compliance on, `aidd validate` warns without them. Each control the change touches has an Acceptance item that proves it. | S4 |
| Specify | The Spec's compliance doc names each control id in its Obligations table with the test or record that proves it, so `aidd record export records --by-control` finds the evidence. | S1, S2, S3 |
| Implement | Deny by default: every new endpoint, object, and admin action checks authorization server side. Secrets come from a secret manager, and CI federates by OIDC with actions pinned by SHA. Nothing sensitive reaches a log. | S4, S5, S6 |
| Implement | Every sign-in, permission change, admin action, and data export writes one audit event (who, what, when, which record, from where). The event goes to an append-only store the product itself cannot rewrite. | S1, S2 |
| Review | Walk each control the change touches in `references/controls.md`; a control the Spec named and the diff does not meet is a finding. | S1, S2 |
| Ship | The security workflow (`aidd-security.yml`: dependency scan, SAST, SBOM, secret scan) is green on the head; the runbook names the breach clocks `aidd-team:incident-response` lists and who starts them. | S5, S7, S3 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dependency scan | no dependency in any lockfile has a known vulnerability | `go run github.com/google/osv-scanner/v2/cmd/osv-scanner@v2.6.0 scan source --recursive --allow-no-lockfiles .`, in `aidd-security.yml` and in `tests` for gate-bound evidence | S5 |
| Static analysis | no injection, unsafe deserialization, or hard-coded secret pattern in the code | `uvx semgrep==1.180.0 scan --config p/default --metrics off --error` | S5, S4 |
| Secret scan | no secret in the working tree or the history | `gitleaks git --redact .` and `gitleaks dir --redact .` (gitleaks v8.30.1), with the base branch's `.gitleaks.toml` on a pull request, in the `secrets` job of `aidd-security.yml` (GitHub) or the `aidd-secrets` job of `aidd-security.gitlab-ci.yml` (GitLab) | S5 |
| Container scan and SBOM | no high or critical vulnerability in a shipped image, and an SBOM for it | `trivy image --exit-code 1 --severity HIGH,CRITICAL <image>` (Trivy v0.74.0) and `syft <image> -o cyclonedx-json` (Syft v1.52.0) | S7, S5 |
| Authorization matrix, one test per cell | each role gets exactly the allow and the deny the matrix states, including across tenants | a parameterized API test generated from the authz matrix rows, in the repository suite | S4, S1 |
| Audit event per admin action | each admin, permission, and export action writes one event with actor, action, target, and time, and the event cannot be updated or deleted | an integration test that performs each action and then tries to update and delete its event as the application's database role | S1, S2 |
| Session and lockout | sign-in locks after the configured failures, a session expires when idle, and the session id rotates at sign-in and on privilege change | API tests with a frozen clock | S4 |

- Breach and incident notification clocks: `aidd-team:incident-response`.
- When a change runs the scans, and least privilege in code: `aidd-team:secure-coding`.

## References

- [references/controls.md](references/controls.md): the unified control set, EC-01 to EC-19. For each control: what the product must do, the test or evidence that proves it, and the SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and GDPR items it serves.
- [references/readiness.md](references/readiness.md): the enterprise-deal checklist (SSO, SCIM, MFA, audit log, admin console, residency, SLA, trust center, VPAT), and the readiness ladder from MVP to certification. Also access management (EC-16): joiner, mover, and leaver, access reviews, break-glass, and service accounts.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/roles.json`.
